title: Sickness Behaviour Explained: Why We Sleep, Lose Appetite & Feel Pain
description:
Ever wondered why you feel fatigued, sleepy, or lose appetite when sick? Science calls this sickness behaviour, and it’s your body’s evolutionary survival strategy. Instead of wasting energy on daily tasks, your immune system pushes you into lethargy, increased sleep, and loss of appetite to conserve energy for fighting infection. Even the pain sensitivity (hyperalgesia) you feel, or the sudden social withdrawal and reduced grooming, are part of this clever design.

This video from Pale Blue Thoughts explains the science of sickness behaviour, from cytokines like IL-1, TNF-alpha, and IL-6 that signal the brain, to how the Vagus nerve acts like a hotline between your immune system and your mood. We explore why fever boosts immunity, why anorexia during illness starves bacteria of iron, and how sleep strengthens your immune cells.

It’s not just humans — animals show it too. Dogs, cats, bats, monkeys, reptiles, and even fish demonstrate sickness behaviour, from bats self-isolating to snakes basking in the sun (behavioural fever). These universal patterns reveal how evolution shaped sickness behaviour across species.

If you’ve searched for why we feel tired when sick, why appetite disappears during illness, why fever is important, or why animals act differently when unwell, this video breaks it all down. By the end, you’ll see that feeling miserable when sick is actually your body’s super-smart healing mechanism, honed over millions of years of evolution.
